q-326461.name: Question 1
q-326461.problem: In an online study, $60%$ of participants reported enjoying painting. Of those, $25%$ said they preferred painting landscapes. What percentage of all participants preferred landscape painting?
q-326461.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the total number of participants.

We're told that $60%$ of participants enjoy painting. Thus, the number of participants who enjoy painting is $0.6x.$

We are also told that of those participants, $25%$ preferred landscapes. So, the number of participants who preferred landscape painting is

$$
0.25(0.6x)=0.15x.
$$

The expression $0.15x$ represents $15%$ of $x.$ Therefore, $15%$ of all participants preferred landscape painting.

q-326465.problem: According to a recent report, $60%$ of tablet owners said they used their tablets regularly. Of those, $50%$ said they used them primarily for drawing. What percentage of all tablet owners used tablets primarily for drawing?
q-326465.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the total number of tablet owners.

We're told that $60%$ of tablet owners used their tablets regularly. Thus, the number of tablet owners who use them regularly is $0.6x.$

q-326900.name: Question 3
q-326900.problem:
A store marked up the price of a jacket to $150%$ of its original cost. The tax on the jacket is $30%$ of its marked-up price.
If the jacket originally cost $$60,$ what is the tax on the jacket?

The tax on the jacket is $$$
{{field-1}}.
q-326900.worked_solution:
First, the marked-up price is $150%$ of the original cost $($60):$

$$
\begin{aligned}150%\times 60 & =\frac{150}{100}\times 60 \\  & =1.5\times 60 \\  & =90\end{aligned}
$$

So, the marked-up price of the jacket is $$90.$
Then, the tax is $30%$ of this price:

$$
\begin{aligned}30%\times 90 & =\frac{30}{100}\times 90 \\  & =0.3\times 90 \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tax on the jacket is $$27.$

q-327532.name: Question 4
q-327532.problem:
A chemist increased the concentration of a lab solution to $125%$ of its original level. An additional reagent then increased that new concentration by $20%.$ If the original concentration was $80$ units, how many additional units were added solely by the reagent?

The reagent added 
{{field-1}}
additional units to the concentration.
q-327532.worked_solution:
First, the new concentration is $125%$ of the original $(80$ units$):$

$$
\begin{aligned}125%\times 80 & =\frac{125}{100}\times 80 \\  & =1.25\times 80 \\  & =100\end{aligned}
$$

So, the new concentration is $100$ units. Then, the increase due to the reagent is $20%$ of this amount:

$$
\begin{aligned}20%\times 100 & =\frac{20}{100}\times 100 \\  & =0.2\times 100 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the reagent added $20$ additional units to the concentration.

q-327544.problem:
An event organizer raised a ticket’s price to $160%$ of its original cost. A tax of $10%$ was applied to the marked-up price. If the ticket originally cost $$75,$ what is the tax?

The tax on the ticket is $$$

First, the marked-up price is $160%$ of the original cost $($75):$

$$
\begin{aligned}160%\times 75 & =\frac{160}{100}\times 75 \\  & =1.6\times 75 \\  & =120\end{aligned}
$$

So, the marked-up price of the ticket is $$120.$ Then, the tax is $10%$ of this price:

$$
\begin{aligned}10%\times 120 & =\frac{10}{100}\times 120 \\  & =0.1\times 120 \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tax on the ticket is $$12.$
